title: Airline tarmac-delay protections
facts: For covered flights at U.S. airports, federal tarmac-delay rules generally require airlines to begin moving an aircraft to a location where passengers can deplane before a domestic tarmac delay exceeds three hours or an international delay exceeds four hours, subject to safety, security and air-traffic-control exceptions.
Airlines generally must provide adequate food and drinking water no later than two hours after a tarmac delay begins, subject to safety or security exceptions.
Operable lavatories and necessary medical attention must be available during covered tarmac delays.
